pr_body:
The inference fields are synthesized from doc_values, regardless of whether the synthetic source is enabled. This change relaxes the translog assertions, allowing inference fields in the same way as we did with the synthetic source.

Relates #120045

Closes #120979
Closes #121007
Closes #120980
Closes #120975
pr_title: Relax translog assertion for inference fields

review_comment:
I think this is ok as a stop-gap.

I wonder if this implies that real-time GET is now more expensive also when there are inference fields? And with this change we now include the inference fields in the real-time GET results?

If so, I wonder if that is the right way to think about inference fields. Given that they are not stored in source, it would possibly make sense to let real-time GET not return them.

I also worry that there could be a discrepancy now where reading real-time GET from translog has inference fields whereas reading from lucene directly does not. Did not check this, thinking you know the answer to it?

Thanks for spotting this, Henning!
We should likely restrict this behavior to TranslogOperationAsserter. The main issue with directly comparing the raw source is that the original _inference_fields may have different precision than the indexed _inference_fields, which is restored from doc values for recovery.

For real-time GET, prior to this change, we relied on source filtering being applied in the [translog reader](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/5bcd170a0bde0c155a36751e034381de3606208c/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/index/engine/TranslogDirectoryReader.java#L523). Therefore, this change isn't technically necessary for real-time GET, as the expectation is to return _source without _inference_fields.

That said, this change doesn’t break existing behavior, since _inference_fields is still removed from _source when parsing the document. The real concern, as you pointed out, is the additional cost of indexing the document just to obtain the pruned source. Given that we’re only removing a single field, this feels unnecessarily expensive.
I'll follow up with a PR with the proposed approach to discuss.
